newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan government backs oil futures market-report.
newsitem.headline: Japan government backs oil futures market-report.

text.p: The Japanese government has drafted a report saying an oil futures market could become an effective means of setting fair market prices in the country, Kyodo news agency said on Saturday.

The Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) and its affiliate Resources and Energy Agency said in a joint report that the U.S. oil futures market had helped introduce transparency in oil prices, Kyodo reported.
It did not say when the report would be issued. MITI and agency officials were not immediately available for comment.
Kyodo said U.S. moves in the early 1980s to lift price regulations on petrol opened the market to newcomers other than oil majors and enlarged the oil spot market in New York.
In turn, the enlarged spot market began to rely heavily on the oil futures market for setting prices.
"There are more voices (in the United States) which praise the oil futures market for its role as a price-setting index rather than for hedging," Kyodo quoted the report as saying.
The report said oil companies in Japan oppose a futures market because such markets in Japan are highly speculative.
But MITI panels will start studying oil futures markets in the United States and Europe in April, Kyodo said.
